description:
Runs 05-13's ticket 1 + ticket 3 model answers TOGETHER as the actual JU0900C/ZA0500 execution chain, to confirm the RPG0907 seen in part05-ju0900c-baseline (docs/probes.md) is gone once both fixes are combined. Compiles solutions/05-13/ju0900c-ticket1.clp (ticket 1: &MINQTY widened to LEN(5 0), matching ZA0500's *ENTRY PLIST - the only change from the as-shipped ju0900c.clp) as &LIB/JU0900C, and solutions/05-13/za0500-ticket3.rpg (ticket 3: adds a program-wide *PSSR; ticket 1's MINQTY bug is deliberately left UNFIXED in this file, per its own header comment) as &LIB/ZA0500 - both overwrite whatever part05-legacy-probe/part05-ju0900c-baseline left in this same &LIB from the as-shipped src/legacy/ sources, which is fine (both those manifests recompile their own copies from src/legacy/ independently on their own connections; this is not a lasting conflict, same self-containment pattern part05-ju0900c-baseline itself already uses). JU0900C hard-codes CALL PGM(&LIB/ZA0500) PARM(&RUNMODE &MINQTY), so za0500-ticket3.rpg has to be compiled AS ZA0500 for the ticket-1-fixed JU0900C to actually reach it - there is no other way to combine the two files as they are written. FIXED in this same session (2026-09-27, found while preparing this manifest, NOT yet hardware-confirmed): solutions/05-13/ju0900c-ticket1.clp had been branched from the as-shipped ju0900c.clp BEFORE that file's own real-hardware CLOF FILE(JUCHUD) -> CPD0043 fix (part05-legacy-probe, docs/probes.md) was applied, so it still carried the same dead-on-arrival compile error (CLOF does not take a FILE keyword). Ported the same fix over in place (see that file's own new header note) rather than leaving a known-broken model answer in solutions/. Each of the two CRTxxxPGM steps below runs DLTPGM first (MONMSG CPF0000) before REPLACE(*YES): a compile failure then leaves the object MISSING instead of silently falling back to whatever object (as-shipped or otherwise) happened to be there already - a stale ZA0500/JU0900C quietly reproducing the OLD RPG0907 would look identical to 'the fix didn't work' if REPLACE(*YES) alone were trusted to signal success. RUNMODE stays '*TEST' (same choice part05-ju0900c-baseline made) so ZAIKOM is never mutated and no TXRESET step is needed afterward - this connection's point is confirming JU0900C's own JUCHUD-order loop now reaches EXCPT for every matched line instead of dying on the first COMP MINQTY, not confirming inventory arithmetic under load. Judge success from the printed OK/SHORT/NOTFOUND lines themselves in the final CALL step's own output (ZA0500's QSYSPRT flows directly into this qsh system() call's stdout - part06-0103-freeform's confirmed finding, already relied on by part05-ju0900c-baseline), NOT merely from the absence of RPG0907/'JU0900C: ZA0500 ended abnormally.': ticket 3's own *PSSR ends with ENDSR '*CANCL', which could in principle end the program quietly on some unrelated exception without JU0900C's own CALL-level MONMSG ever firing, and that would look like silent success too. expected/notes.md in this directory carries the prediction (12 lines: 10 OK, 2 SHORT, 0 NOTFOUND) already hand-computed in part05-ju0900c-baseline's own expected/notes.md for 'if ticket 1's bug were absent' - reused as-is here, since db/data/load_v1.sql and ZAIKOM are unchanged by every manifest that has connected so far (all *TEST-mode runs; this one too). A collect step re-reads JUCHUD's own row count (expected 12) as a mechanical cross-check against the number of printed lines - it executes AFTER the whole CL wrapper regardless of its position in this JSON array (verify/lib/batch.mjs: collect steps always run last, once per connection), so its placement here is for readability only, not real ordering. Also compiles, registers and runs TXCHECK (05-13's own exercise) as an object-existence smoke test: recreates TXCKM (self-contained, in case this &LIB has none yet - same DLTF/CRTPF pattern as part05-txcheck-probe), deletes then inserts this lesson's own two rows (ZA0500, JU0900C - same SEQNBR/CKDESC docs/part05/05-13-checkpoint-tickets.md itself specifies), recompiles TXCHECK, and calls it via the CALL PGM(...) PARM(...) form (V2-confirmed per docs/probes.md; the *CMD wrapper tools/qcmdsrc/txcheck.cmd is still unconfirmed, so this manifest deliberately avoids it, per this session's own instructions). TXCHECK only proves the two objects exist with the right type (v1 scope, per its own header comment) - it does NOT prove the ticket 1/3 fixes are logically correct; the OK/SHORT/NOTFOUND row check above is what actually confirms that. Running TXCHECK before the combined CALL also means a compile failure on either JU0900C or ZA0500 shows up as a TXCHECK FAIL before the riskier step is even reached. Ticket 2 (solutions/05-13/ticket2-notes.md) is OUT OF SCOPE for this manifest: that file's own title says a compilable model answer does not exist yet ('コンパイル可能なソースはまだ無い'), and this manifest deliberately does not write one - ticket 2 stays untested until a future session actually writes and hardware-confirms a JU0900C/ZA0500 (or OPNQRYF JFILE) rewrite for it. The combined JU0900C->ZA0500 CALL is placed last (README.md's own hang-risk-last rule) since this exact ticket1+ticket3 object combination has never been executed before; TXCHECK's own CALL is placed earlier because it is already V2-confirmed (part05-txcheck-probe, reused in part07-05-checkpoint) and carries no comparable risk. Prerequisite: TXSETUP has already built the sample DB (ZAIKOM/JUCHUD/JUCHUM) in this library, same prerequisite as part05-legacy-probe/part05-ju0900c-baseline - run from a branch where solutions/05-13/ and this manifest both exist, not main. RUNTXRESET (`&LIB/TXRESET LIB(&LIB)`, a pre-existing, already hardware-confirmed *CMD - docs/probes.md:219/418, same invocation part06-0509-procs-files/part07-05-checkpoint already rely on) runs FIRST, before any compile, for a reason specific to this shared dev-role &LIB: a sibling manifest under design in this same session (verify/part05-mch1202-corrupt) deliberately plants a JUNO='C05119' row into JUCHUD/JUCHUM and leaves it there on purpose (its own description says so explicitly), and EBCDIC 'C' sorts before 'J', so that row would read FIRST in JU0900C's own OPNQRYF KEYFLD((JUNO)(JULINE)) order if it were still present - silently invalidating both the 12-row/10-OK/2-SHORT prediction in expected/notes.md and the 'every manifest so far is *TEST, data unchanged' premise this description relies on elsewhere. Running TXRESET first makes this manifest correct regardless of which order these two sibling manifests actually connect in, rather than depending on a coordination promise. The two collect steps below (a full JUCHUD row dump and a JUCHUM JUNO list, replacing a bare COUNT(*)) exist for the same reason: a stray 'C05119' row would be visible on its own in these results even if the TXRESET-first defense above were somehow bypassed (e.g. a future edit removes it). On the *PSSR/ENDSR('*CANCL') question this description raises above (whether a silently-canceled ZA0500 could be mistaken for success): part05-qcmdexc-runtime's own actual (local, gitignored) result file already answers this for the identical ENDSR('*CANCL') mechanism za0500-ticket3.rpg reuses from za0510.rpg - its vfylog reads 'Error RPG0000 caused program ZA0510V to stop.' followed by 'RUNZA1V FAILED.', i.e. ENDSR('*CANCL') does NOT let the program return to its caller unnoticed; it raises a genuine RPG-class escape that a broad MONMSG (CPF0000, which also matches the CPF9999 function-check an unmonitored RPG-class escape gets wrapped into one level up, exactly as part05-ju0900c-baseline's own RPG0907->RPG9001->CPF9999 chain already showed) does catch. So if za0500-ticket3.rpg's *PSSR were to fire during this run, JU0900C's own existing MONMSG around its CALL PGM(&LIB/ZA0500) step would very likely print 'JU0900C: ZA0500 ended abnormally.' - making the ABSENCE of that message, together with 12 printed OK/SHORT/NOTFOUND rows, solid secondary evidence, not merely a caveat. What remains genuinely open (not yet observed on real hardware by any prior connection): whether ZA0500's own QSYSPRT actually flows into this qsh system() call's stdout at all - part06-0103-freeform confirmed this qsh behavior for a different program, and part05-ju0900c-baseline's own connection never actually saw a single printed row (RPG0907 fired before ZA0500's first EXCPT), so this manifest is the first real chance to see ZA0500 rows in the 'run' section's own output. If the run shows 0 printed lines together with DONE, no RPG0907, no 'ended abnormally', and TXCHECK's 2 PASS lines, expected/notes.md's reading guide below now lists 'the print channel itself may not carry ZA0500's QSYSPRT' as the FIRST hypothesis to rule out, ahead of 'a *PSSR fired silently' (which the RUNZA1V/RPG0000 evidence above argues against).

2026-09-27 REVISIONS (two-reviewer critique of this manifest's first draft, addressed by actually editing this file rather than a follow-up note): (1) INSTXCKM's own RUNSQL INSERT now monitors SQL0000 in addition to CPF0000, matching DELTXCKM immediately above it and this repo's own established convention for every RUNSQL step touching TXCKM elsewhere (verify/lib/clgen.mjs's own internal VFYLOG DELETE/INSERT calls, part07-05-checkpoint's SEEDTXCKM) - a SQL-class *ESCAPE from INSTXCKM alone, previously uncaught at the step level, would have been caught one level up by this wrapper's own program-level MONMSG(CPF0000, GOTO FAILSAFE) and skipped CPTXCHK/RUNTXCHK/RUNCOMBO/RUNZA0500H entirely, silently spending this library's one-connection-at-a-time budget on nothing. (2) CPTXCKM no longer unconditionally DLTF+CRTPFs &LIB/TXCKM (part05-txcheck-probe's original pattern) - TXCKM is a persistent, shared ledger other lessons' manifests also write rows into in this same dev-role &LIB (part07-05-checkpoint's SEEDTXCKM already registers 07-05's own 3 rows there), so an unconditional DLTF here would silently destroy any such rows a sibling manifest had already written before this one connects. Switched to the same non-destructive CHKOBJ+conditional-CRTPF idiom part07-05-checkpoint's own CPTXCKM step already uses (build only if missing, touch nothing if it already exists) - DELTXCKM immediately below it already only ever deletes this lesson's OWN rows (LESSON='05-13'), so this was the one step actually contradicting that self-restraint. (3) Added ZA0500H (compiled from src/za0500h.clp, a new verify-local helper, NOT part of the curriculum) and its own CALL step (RUNZA0500H): ticket 1's own grading rubric (docs/part05/05-13-checkpoint-tickets.md) explicitly asks for the SAME result confirmed both via a plain test harness AND via JU0900C - two independent call paths agreeing - and this manifest previously only exercised the JU0900C-mediated path. ZA0500H opens JUCHUD/JUCHUM the same way ju0900c-ticket1.clp does and CALLs &LIB/ZA0500 directly with a properly DCL'd *DEC LEN(5 0) &MINQTY, RUNMODE hard-coded '*TEST' - its own printed OK/SHORT/NOTFOUND lines should be byte-for-byte identical to RUNCOMBO's (same unchanged data, same RUNMODE, same correctly-typed MINQTY=5). RUNZA0500H is placed AFTER RUNCOMBO, not before it (2026-09-27, advisor-flagged ordering risk): both steps open JUCHUD via their own OPNQRYF, and neither ZA0500H nor ju0900c-ticket1.clp explicitly closes that open data path with a scoped CLOF before returning (the as-shipped CLOF FILE(JUCHUD) line was a compile error and was REMOVED, not replaced with a scoped close - see that file's own header note). work/design/refs/ileconcepts75.txt (lines 6248-6255) states that for an OPM program (which both ZA0500H and JU0900C are) running in the default activation group, an ODP opened via OPNQRYF is scoped to the CALL-LEVEL NUMBER, not the whole job - meaning it should already be torn down automatically once the opening program's own top-level CALL returns to this wrapper, well before the next step's CALL begins. This has NOT been confirmed against a real OPNQRYF-specific case on this hardware, so this manifest still runs RUNCOMBO (the headline ticket-1+ticket-3 confirmation) FIRST: if the ODP-scoping reasoning above turns out to be wrong for some reason specific to this case, the failure mode is 'RUNZA0500H (the lower-priority parity check) can't open JUCHUD and reports so cleanly' rather than losing the headline result. See expected/notes.md for how to read a 'ZA0500H: could not open JUCHUD.' message under this hypothesis. (4) This manifest's own RUNCOMBO step runs ONLY against clean data (za0500-ticket3.rpg's own *PSSR is never expected to fire here - see expected/notes.md's own precondition table), so it does NOT exercise ticket 3's actual *PSSR/QCMDEXC/CHGDTAARA path at all, despite this description's earlier framing spending most of its length reasoning about what would happen IF the *PSSR fired. That reasoning stays here as a precondition check (it argues the *PSSR did NOT fire, which is the expected outcome on clean data), but it must not be mistaken for having exercised ticket 3's fix - a companion connection, verify/part05-13-pssr, deliberately corrupts a JUCHUD row (05-11's own C0511S technique) and reads the *LDA(21,20) flag back in-job specifically to observe the *PSSR actually firing; that is the connection ticket 3's own 再現確認 rubric item is answered by, not this one. (5) tools/qclsrc/txcheck.clp's own SUMMARY label sends 'N passed, ' and 'N failed.' as two SEPARATE SNDPGMMSG calls (two distinct job-log lines), not the single combined line docs/part05/05-13-checkpoint-tickets.md's own step 4 describes; moreover the actual, ALREADY-OBSERVED shape (work/verify/results/part05-txcheck-probe-2026-09-26T13-31-16-153Z.json and .../part07-05-checkpoint-2026-09-27T03-31-30-435Z.json, both real hardware job-log dumps from this session) shows the counts as 10-digit zero-padded numeric strings ('0000000003 passed,' / '0000000000 failed.'), not plain digits - CHGVAR from *DEC LEN(5 0) to *CHAR LEN(10) zero-pads, and %TRIM only strips surrounding blanks, not leading zeros. See expected/notes.md's reading guide for the actual (split, zero-padded) shape this connection should show in VFYLOG, and this description flags the lesson-text/actual-output mismatch (both the line split and the digit formatting) as a known discrepancy for a future session to fix (either merge TXCHECK's two SNDPGMMSGs into one and avoid the zero-padded conversion, or correct the lesson text).

steps.label: CPJU0900C
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/JU0900C)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/JU0900C) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(JU0900C) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPZA0500
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/ZA0500)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTRPGPGM PGM(&LIB/ZA0500) SRCFILE(&LIB/QRPGSRC) SRCMBR(ZA0500) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPZA0500H
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/ZA0500H)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/ZA0500H) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(ZA0500H) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPTXCKM
steps.cmd:
CHKOBJ OBJ(&LIB/TXCKM) OBJTYPE(*FILE)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF9801) EXEC(CRTPF FILE(&LIB/TXCKM) SRCFILE(&LIB/QDDSSRC) SRCMBR(TXCKM))

steps.label: DELTXCKM
steps.cmd: RUNSQL SQL('DELETE FROM &LIB/TXCKM WHERE LESSON = ''05-13''') COMMIT(*NONE)

steps.label: INSTXCKM
steps.cmd: RUNSQL SQL('INSERT INTO &LIB/TXCKM (LESSON, SEQNBR, OBJNAME, OBJTYPE, OBJATTR, CKDESC) VALUES (''05-13'', 10, ''ZA0500'', ''*PGM'', '' '', ''ZA0500 still exists and compiles''), (''05-13'', 20, ''JU0900C'', ''*PGM'', '' '', ''JU0900C still exists and compiles'')') COMMIT(*NONE)

steps.sql: SELECT JUNO, JULINE, JUSHO, JUSU FROM &LIB/JUCHUD ORDER BY JUNO, JULINE
SELECT JUNO FROM &LIB/JUCHUM ORDER BY JUNO
